title: Coupled Penrose vanishing on the round four-sphere

items.title: Positive incidence geometry for the coupled Penrose transform
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Let $S^4=\{X\in\mathbb R^5:|X|=1\}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\setminus\{\infty\}\cong\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\wedge dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=0}^3dx_\mu^2$. Define the Wirtinger derivatives on this chart by

$$\partial_{z_1}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x_0}-i\partial_{x_1}),\quad \partial_{\bar z_1}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x_0}+i\partial_{x_1}),\quad \partial_{z_2}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x_2}-i\partial_{x_3}),\quad \partial_{\bar z_2}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x_2}+i\partial_{x_3});$$

These vector fields act on the complexification of the real tangent bundle. Fix the antiunitary right quaternionic structure $j:\mathbb C^4\to\mathbb C^4$ in these coordinates by

$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1).$$

Thus $j$ is conjugate-linear, preserves the standard Hermitian norm, and satisfies $j^2=-I$. Put $\mathbb H^2=\mathbb C^4$ with this right quaternionic structure, $Z=\mathbb CP^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\pi:Z\to\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\pi(\ell)=\ell+j\ell$ for each complex line $\ell\subset\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\cong\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$

and the fibre over infinity is $L_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\mathbb C^4$, and give $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$, the tautological holomorphic line bundle, its induced Hermitian metric; $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$ has the tensor-square metric. On the incidence chart $\lambda_1\ne0$, set $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $\mu_1/\lambda_1=z_1-\bar z_2t$, and $\mu_2/\lambda_1=z_2+\bar z_1t$. Write $T^{0,1}Z$ for the $-i$ eigensubbundle of the complexified tangent endomorphism determined by the complex structure. The constant-$t$ horizontal complex directions of type $(0,1)$ are spanned by

$$H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2},\qquad H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1};$$

They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates and, together with $\partial_{\bar t}$, form a direct local frame of $T^{0,1}Z$. Define $V^{0,1}=\ker(d\pi)\cap T^{0,1}Z$ and let $H^{0,1}$ be its Fubini–Study orthogonal complement in $T^{0,1}Z$. The complex alpha-plane at $\ell\in L_x$ is the two-dimensional complex subspace $d\pi_\ell(H^{0,1}_\ell)\subset T_xS^4\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$; it is also the image under $d\pi_\ell$ of the span of $H_1,H_2$. These constant-$t$ chart lifts project to the same alpha-plane as the global metric-horizontal lifts, although they may differ from them by vertical components. Global horizontal/vertical form decompositions use the Fubini–Study orthogonal splitting; local computations may use the displayed constant-$t$ splitting after retaining the resulting frame and normalization factors. The second projective chart gives the same alpha-plane at $t=\infty$.

items.title: Incidence alpha planes detect positive-orientation anti-self-duality
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle and let $A$ be a smooth connection on $E$, with curvature $F_A=\nabla_A^2\in\Omega^2(S^4,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}E)$. For real two-forms $\eta,\zeta$, let $*_g$ be the Hodge star characterized by $\eta\wedge *_g\zeta=\langle\eta,\zeta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$, and extend it complex-linearly to the form factor of $F_A$. At a finite point of the positively oriented stereographic chart in the incidence geometry, evaluate $F_A$ complex-bilinearly on $H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2}$ and $H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1}$. Then $F_A(H_1,H_2)=0$ for every $t\in\mathbb C$ if and only if the self-dual part $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ vanishes at that point. The same equivalence holds at the omitted projective value $t=\infty$ by using the second incidence chart.

items.title: Dolbeault groups of the negative twistor-fibre twists
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Let $L=\mathbb CP^1$ and let $\mathcal O_L(k)$ be the degree-$k$ holomorphic line bundle. For the smooth Dolbeault complexes on $L$, the cohomology groups satisfy

$$H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-1))=H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-1))=H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-2))=0,\qquad H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-2))\cong\mathbb C.$$

The canonical bundle $K_L:=\Lambda^{1,0}T^*L$ is the holomorphic cotangent line bundle, whose fibre at $p\in L$ is the complex-linear dual of $T_p^{1,0}L$, the $+i$ eigenspace of the complex structure on the complexified tangent space. It satisfies $K_L\cong\mathcal O_L(-2)$; the last group is one-dimensional, and the first three vanish.

items.title: Injective fibre-harmonic edge for coupled Penrose cohomology
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Assume full AC and the following analytic comparison: for $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, every finite-rank holomorphic vector bundle $G$ on $X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ has a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,\mathcal O(G))\cong H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,G)$ for every $q\ge0$, and for $G=\mathcal O_X$ one has $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathbb C$ and $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ for $q>0$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank Hermitian bundle with smooth unitary connection $A$. On the incidence fibration $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$, let $F$ be a finite-rank holomorphic bundle and fix an isometric smooth identification $F\cong\pi^*E$ under which the component of its Dolbeault operator on $V^{0,1}=\ker(d\pi)\cap T^{0,1}Z$ is the ordinary coefficientwise vertical Dolbeault operator and its component on the Fubini–Study orthogonal horizontal subbundle $H^{0,1}$ is $\nabla_A$ evaluated on the projected complex alpha-plane. Give $F$ the pulled-back Hermitian metric from $E$, give $\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ its induced tensor-square Fubini–Study metric, and use the product metric on $F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ and the induced Fubini–Study metric and volume on each fibre $L_x$.

Write $H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ for analytic sheaf cohomology of the holomorphic section sheaf, identified by the stated comparison with the smooth Dolbeault quotient

$$H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2)):=\frac{\ker(\bar\partial_F:\Omega^{0,1}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\to\Omega^{0,2}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2)))}{\operatorname{im}(\bar\partial_F:\Omega^{0,0}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\to\Omega^{0,1}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2)))}.$$

For $x\in S^4$, let $Q_x\subset\mathbb C^4$ be the quaternionic two-plane corresponding to $x$. Its quaternionic Hermitian structure determines the alternating form $\delta_x\in\Lambda^2Q_x^*$ by $\delta_x(v,jv)=1$ for every unit vector $v\in Q_x$. Under $K_{L_x}=\Lambda^{1,0}T^*L_x\cong\det(Q_x)^*\otimes\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2)$, let $\iota_x:\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2)\to K_{L_x}$ be multiplication by $\delta_x$. The fibre Dolbeault groups include $H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-1))=H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-1))=H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2))=0$ and $H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal H_x^{0,1}\subset\Omega^{0,1}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2))$ be the kernel of the fibre Dolbeault Laplacian $\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$ for the induced metrics. Compact Hodge decomposition identifies $\mathcal H_x^{0,1}$ with $H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L_x,\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2))$, so this harmonic space is one-dimensional. Let $\sigma_x\in\mathcal H_x^{0,1}$ be the unique form satisfying $\int_{L_x}\iota_x(\sigma_x)=1$. Let $\sigma$ be the resulting smooth vertical $(0,1)$-form on $Z$, extended to vanish on $H^{0,1}$. For a global closed representative $\alpha\in\Omega^{0,1}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$, let $\Pi_x$ be the orthogonal projection of $\Omega^{0,1}(L_x,E_x\otimes\mathcal O_{L_x}(-2))$ onto its fibrewise Dolbeault-harmonic subspace, and define $\mathcal P_A[\alpha](x)=s(x)$ by $\Pi_x(\alpha|_{L_x})=s(x)\otimes\sigma_x$. This gives a linear map

$$\mathcal P_A:H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\longrightarrow\Gamma(S^4,E).$$

Every such $\alpha$ has a unique decomposition $\alpha=\alpha_H+s\sigma+\bar\partial_F\gamma$, where $s=\mathcal P_A[\alpha]$, $\alpha_H\in\Omega^{0,1}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ annihilates $V^{0,1}$, and $\gamma\in\Omega^{0,0}(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ is smooth on all of $Z$. The map is well defined and injective. The comparison is supplied by the local analytic Dolbeault-resolution theorem; no algebraic-to-analytic comparison is assumed.

items.title: Coupled Penrose vanishing on the round four-sphere
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $S^4$ have the unit round metric and the positive stereographic orientation for $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle with a positive Hermitian metric $h$ and a smooth connection $\nabla_A$ preserving $h$. Its curvature is $F_A=\nabla_A^2\in\Omega^2(S^4,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}E)$. For real two-forms $\eta,\zeta$, let $*_g$ be characterized by $\eta\wedge *_g\zeta=\langle\eta,\zeta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$, and extend it complex-linearly on the form factor of $F_A$. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and assume $F_A^+=0$, the anti-self-duality condition in this orientation. On $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ use homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ and the incidence equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$, with infinity fibre $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$; these fibres define the incidence projection $\pi:Z\to S^4$. On $\lambda_1\ne0$, put $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2}$, and $H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1}$. The projected complex alpha-plane at $[\lambda]\in\pi^{-1}(x)$ is $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{d\pi(H_1),d\pi(H_2)\}$; the second projective chart covers $t=\infty$. Let $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ be the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$. Suppose $F$ is a finite-rank holomorphic bundle (locally trivial with holomorphic transition maps), smoothly identified with $\pi^*E$, and its Dolbeault operator is the coefficientwise ordinary vertical operator and the connection $\nabla_A$ on the projected complex alpha-planes. For a finite-rank holomorphic bundle $G\to Z$, write $H^1(Z,G)$ for analytic sheaf cohomology of its holomorphic-section sheaf; under the analytic Dolbeault comparison it is canonically $\ker(\bar\partial_G:\Omega^{0,1}(Z,G)\to\Omega^{0,2}(Z,G))/\operatorname{im}(\bar\partial_G:\Omega^{0,0}(Z,G)\to\Omega^{0,1}(Z,G))$, where $\Omega^{0,q}(Z,G)$ denotes the global smooth $G$-valued $(0,q)$-forms. Write $F^\vee$ for the fibrewise complex dual. Then

$$H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=H^1(Z,F^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=0.$$

This applies to arbitrary reducible and flat summands. It assumes no algebraic-to-analytic GAGA, monad, or inverse ADHM normal form as an independent premise.

items.title: Flat summands in coupled Penrose vanishing
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: Assume full AC and use $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ with $\pi:Z\to S^4$ the fixed incidence fibration: its finite fibres in the positively oriented stereographic chart satisfy $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$ and $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$, and its fibre at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. Let $E_0\to S^4$ be any smooth finite-rank Hermitian bundle with a smooth unitary connection $A_0$ whose curvature obeys $F_{A_0}^+=(F_{A_0}+*_gF_{A_0})/2=0$. Let $F_0$ be a finite-rank holomorphic bundle smoothly isometrically identified with $\pi^*E_0$ whose Dolbeault operator has the coefficientwise vertical Dolbeault component and the component $\nabla_{A_0}$ along the projected complex alpha-planes. For any integer $m\ge0$, set $E=E_0\oplus(S^4\times\mathbb C^m)$ with the direct-sum Hermitian metric and connection $A=A_0\oplus d$, and set $F=F_0\oplus\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}$ with the induced holomorphic Dolbeault operator and direct-sum metric. Then $H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=H^1(Z,F^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=0$. For the fibre-harmonic projection defined by the induced Fubini–Study and product metrics, the transform and its dual decompose as $\mathcal P_A=\mathcal P_{A_0}\oplus\mathcal P_d$; the second summand acts componentwise on the trivial rank-$m$ bundle. Thus adjoining any finite flat summand preserves the coupled vanishing conclusion, including $m=0$.

items.title: Local transforms versus global injectivity
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: Let $U_N$ and $U_S$ be the two stereographic charts of $S^4$, and let $\xi\in H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ be a global class under the coupled theorem's hypotheses. On each chart compute the fibre-harmonic section from a global closed Dolbeault representative. On $U_N\cap U_S$ the two local sections agree because they are the harmonic projection on the same fibre and are unchanged by replacing the representative by a Dolbeault-exact form. If the glued section is zero, the global class is zero by injectivity. Thus a local contour expression alone establishes neither compatibility on the overlap nor injectivity of the global class map.
